stories.headline: US-Iran Islamabad Peace Talks End Without Deal After 21 Hours Over Nuclear Impasse

key_facts.fact: US Vice President JD Vance announced the talks ended without agreement after 21 hours, saying Iran refused to commit to not developing nuclear weapons.
key_facts.excerpt: "The bad news is that we have not reached an agreement... The simple fact is that we need to see an affirmative commitment that they will not seek a nuclear weapon, and they will not seek the tools that would enable them to quickly achieve a nuclear weapon."

key_facts.fact: The talks were the first face-to-face engagement between the US and Iran since 2015, and the highest-level discussions since the 1979 Islamic Revolution.
key_facts.excerpt: It was the first face-to-face engagement between the U.S. and Iran since 2015, when the Obama administration negotiated a nuclear deal with Iran that was later scrapped by Trump.

key_facts.fact: Iran demanded release of $6 billion in frozen assets, guarantees around its nuclear program, the right to charge ships through the Strait of Hormuz, and an end to Israeli strikes on Hezbollah in Lebanon.
key_facts.excerpt: Other demands from the Iranian delegation included the release of $6 billion in frozen assets, guarantees around its nuclear program and the right to charge ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

key_facts.fact: Vance left a 'final and best offer' on the table, saying 'We'll see if the Iranians accept it,' leaving a narrow path for a future agreement.
key_facts.excerpt: "We leave here with a very simple proposal: a method of understanding that is our final and best offer... We'll see if the Iranians accept it."

key_facts.fact: The war has killed at least 3,000 people in Iran, 2,020 in Lebanon, 23 in Israel, and more than a dozen in Gulf Arab states since US-Israeli strikes began on Feb. 28.
key_facts.excerpt: The war has killed at least 3,000 people in Iran, 2,020 in Lebanon, 23 in Israel and more than a dozen in Gulf Arab states, and caused lasting damage to infrastructure in half a dozen Middle Eastern countries.

key_facts.fact: Chinese, Egyptian, Saudi and Qatari officials were in Islamabad to indirectly facilitate the talks, reflecting the global stakes of the negotiations.
key_facts.excerpt: Reflecting the high stakes, officials from the region said Chinese, Egyptian, Saudi and Qatari officials were in Islamabad to indirectly facilitate the talks.

stories.headline: US Navy Transits Strait of Hormuz for First Time Since Iran War Began, Starts Mine Clearing

key_facts.fact: Two US Navy guided-missile destroyers passed through the Strait of Hormuz on April 11, the first American warship transit since the Iran war began six weeks ago.
key_facts.excerpt: Minutes before Trump's post, reports started to emerge about the presence of U.S. Navy ships in the strait.

key_facts.fact: Trump posted on Truth Social that the US has started clearing the strait and that 'all 28' of Iran's mine-dropping boats 'are lying at the bottom of the sea.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We're now starting the process of clearing out the Strait of Hormuz," Trump wrote in a Truth Social post, adding that "all 28" of Iran's "mine dropper boats are also lying at the bottom of the sea."

key_facts.fact: Iranian state TV denied any US ships had crossed the strait. Iran's military command denied reports about the passage.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's state media, however, earlier said Iran forced a U.S. military ship that was attempting to cross the strait to turn around.

key_facts.fact: The strait's effective closure for ~40 days has disrupted global energy markets and sent oil and gasoline prices soaring, despite most oil flowing through it not going to the US.
key_facts.excerpt: Fear of Iranian attacks on shipping over the past several weeks has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, a critical conduit for global oil supplies. Throttling the strait has disrupted global energy markets.

key_facts.fact: Three Liberian- and Chinese-flagged supertankers also passed through the strait on Saturday, the first commercial vessels to exit the Gulf since the ceasefire last week.
key_facts.excerpt: Three Liberian- and Chinese-flagged supertankers did pass through the strait today, shipping data showed, marking what appeared to be the first vessels to exit the Gulf since last week's US-Iran ceasefire.

stories.headline: US Intel: China Preparing to Ship Air Defense Weapons to Iran via Third Countries

key_facts.fact: US intelligence indicates China is preparing to deliver shoulder-fired anti-air missile systems (MANPADs) to Iran within weeks, according to three people familiar with intelligence assessments.
key_facts.excerpt: The systems Beijing is preparing to transfer are shoulder-fired anti-air missile systems known as MANPADs, the sources said, which posed an asymmetric threat to low-flying US military aircraft throughout the course of the five-week war.

key_facts.fact: Beijing is working to route shipments through third countries to mask their origin, two sources said. This would mark an escalation from dual-use technology to direct weapons transfers.
key_facts.excerpt: Two of the sources told CNN there are indications that Beijing is working to route the shipments through third countries to mask their true origin.

key_facts.fact: Trump warned China would face consequences: 'If China does that, China will have big problems, OK?' He is scheduled to visit Beijing next month for talks with Xi Jinping.
key_facts.excerpt: Asked by CNN on Saturday about the US intelligence and whether he has spoken to Xi about the issue, Trump indicated that Beijing would face consequences if it sent weapons to Tehran. "If China does that, China will have big problems, OK?" he said.

key_facts.fact: Chinese Embassy denied the claim: 'China has never provided weapons to any party to the conflict; the information in question is untrue.'
key_facts.excerpt: "China has never provided weapons to any party to the conflict; the information in question is untrue," Liu Pengyu, a spokesman for the Chinese diplomatic mission in the United States, told TASS.

key_facts.fact: The intelligence suggests Iran may be using the ceasefire to replenish weapons with help from foreign partners. A US F-15 was shot down over Iran last week reportedly by a 'handheld shoulder missile.'
key_facts.excerpt: Trump indicated during a press conference on Monday that the F-15 fighter jet shot down over Iran last week was hit by a 'handheld shoulder missile, [a] heat-seeking missile,' and Tehran said it had used a 'new' air defense system.

sources.title: Exclusive: US intelligence indicates China is preparing weapons shipment to Iran amid fragile ceasefire
China denies plans to supply air defense systems to Iran

stories.headline: Ukraine and Russia Swap 175 POWs Each, Begin 32-Hour Orthodox Easter Ceasefire

key_facts.fact: Ukraine and Russia exchanged 175 prisoners of war each on April 11, with Ukraine also receiving 7 civilians from Russian captivity. Most Ukrainian servicemen had been held since 2022.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine and Russia exchanged 175 prisoners of war each on Saturday in their latest swap... He said the Ukrainian servicemen had defended the country on different fronts from the east to the south and most of them had been in captivity in Russia since 2022.

key_facts.fact: The United Arab Emirates mediated the exchange. Russia also returned 7 civilians originally from the Kursk region.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia's Defence Ministry said the United Arab Emirates had mediated the exchange. Russia took back 175 servicemen and also seven civilians originally from the Kursk region.

key_facts.fact: A 32-hour Easter ceasefire began at 4 p.m. local time (1300 GMT) on Saturday and was set to end at midnight on Sunday, as both countries celebrate Orthodox Easter.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia said the ceasefire would begin at 4 p.m. (1300 GMT) on Saturday and end at midnight on Sunday.

key_facts.fact: 163 of the freed Ukrainians had been held since 2022, marking over four years in captivity. Some had difficulty walking and were transported by ambulance.
key_facts.excerpt: Andrii Yusov, a Ukrainian defence intelligence representative, said 163 of those freed had been held since 2022. "This is a real success, a very significant achievement."

key_facts.fact: US-brokered peace talks between Ukraine and Russia remain stalled over the issue of territory. POW exchanges are among the few concrete results from those negotiations.
key_facts.excerpt: They are among the few concrete results to emerge from several rounds of U.S.-brokered peace talks between Ukraine and Russia, which remain stalled over the issue of territory.

sources.title: Ukraine, Russia swap 175 servicemen each ahead of Easter ceasefire

stories.headline: Hungary Votes in Landmark Election That Could End Orbán's 16-Year Grip on Power

key_facts.fact: Hungary holds parliamentary elections on April 12 in what is seen as PM Viktor Orbán's biggest political test in 16 years of rule. Challenger Péter Magyar's Tisza party leads by double digits in most independent polls.
key_facts.excerpt: Prime Minister Viktor Orbán is facing the biggest political test of his career as his challenger Péter Magyar's center-right Tisza party has charted a meteoric rise and is leading by double digits in most independent polls.

key_facts.fact: Magyar, 45, is a former member of Fidesz's inner circle and ex-husband of Orbán's justice minister. He burst into prominence in 2024 during a presidential pardon scandal.
key_facts.excerpt: Magyar burst into prominence in 2024 as the government faced a presidential pardon scandal that involved a child abuser's accomplice.

key_facts.fact: Orbán has campaigned on external dangers including the Ukraine war and his close relationship with Trump. VP Vance made a two-day visit to Budapest earlier in the campaign.
key_facts.excerpt: Orbán's campaign has been plagued by Hungary's poor economic performance, revelations of the government's increasingly close connections to Russia and corruption allegations. He has sought to boost his appeal with voters by emphasizing his close relationship with U.S. President Donald Trump.

key_facts.fact: The election is closely watched internationally. An Orbán defeat would impact the network of right-wing parties across Europe and the transatlantic relationship, given his ties to both Putin and Trump.
key_facts.excerpt: As a friend to both Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump, there is much international attention on the country's 12 April elections.

key_facts.fact: Magyar promises EU reengagement and unfreezing billions in EU funds withheld from Hungary, while his supporters chanted 'Európa! Európa!' at his final rally in Debrecen.
key_facts.excerpt: As his supporters waved national flags and chanted "Európa! Európa!" in University Square, Magyar said that "many millions" of voters would show on Sunday that "Hungary's place was, is, and will be in Europe."

stories.headline: Japan Approves Additional $4B for Rapidus, Bringing Total State Investment to $16.3B

key_facts.fact: Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) approved ¥631.5 billion ($4B) in additional subsidies for Rapidus on April 11, bringing cumulative R&D support to ¥2.354 trillion ($14.8B).
key_facts.excerpt: Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) formally decided on April 11 to provide an additional ¥631.5 billion (approximately $4.0 billion) in support for fiscal year 2026 to Rapidus.

key_facts.fact: Total state investment and fees will reach ¥2.6 trillion ($16.3B) by end of FY2027. The funds will bankroll work for Fujitsu, one of Rapidus's first customers.
key_facts.excerpt: The ministry also said that NEDO has decided to support semiconductor design-related projects by Fujitsu and IBM Japan.

key_facts.fact: Rapidus targets mass production of 2-nanometer chips by FY2027. An analysis center and R&D base opened in Chitose City, Hokkaido, on the same day.
key_facts.excerpt: Rapidus held an opening ceremony for a newly built semiconductor analysis center and R&D base adjacent to its own factory in Chitose City, Hokkaido.

key_facts.fact: METI Minister Ryosei Akazawa attended the opening and said 'We will spare no necessary support for the success of the plan.' Rapidus CEO pledged to meet the 2027 mass production target.
key_facts.excerpt: METI Minister Ryosei Akazawa stated, "We will spare no necessary support for the success of the plan," reiterating the government's strong commitment.

key_facts.fact: Rapidus still lags significantly behind TSMC, which began mass-producing 2nm chips in 2025. Rapidus plans an IPO around FY2031 and aims to raise ¥3 trillion in private funding.
key_facts.excerpt: Rapidus is working on the development of next-generation logic semiconductors at the 2-nanometre scale and plans to start mass production in the fiscal year 2027.

sources.title: Japan Approves Over ¥630 Billion in Additional Support for Rapidus to Mass-Produce Domestic 2nm Semiconductors

stories.headline: SpaceX Launches Cygnus XL to ISS Carrying East Africa's First Climate Camera

key_facts.fact: SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 carrying Northrop Grumman's Cygnus XL cargo ship to the ISS from Cape Canaveral at 7:41 a.m. EDT on April 11, delivering over 5,000 kg (11,000 lbs) of supplies and experiments.
key_facts.excerpt: The April 11 SpaceX carrying NG-24 mission at 7:41 a.m. from Launch Complex 40. The Falcon 9 is sending a Northrop Grumman Cygnus XL cargo spacecraft to the space station.

key_facts.fact: The payload includes ClimCam, a joint Earth-observation camera from Kenya, Uganda, and Egypt — the first climate-focused instrument from East Africa to reach the ISS.
key_facts.excerpt: ClimCam is a joint initiative involving the Kenya Space Agency, the Egyptian Space Agency, and the Uganda National Space Programme, underscoring growing regional cooperation in space technology.

key_facts.fact: ClimCam uses multispectral imaging combined with AI to generate near-real-time climate and weather data, targeting floods, droughts, and extreme weather in East Africa.
key_facts.excerpt: The system utilizes multispectral imaging combined with artificial intelligence to generate near-real-time climate and weather data.

key_facts.fact: The camera will be installed on the Airbus-operated Bartolomeo platform on the ISS Columbus module and operate for 6-12 months. The project was selected via a UN Office for Outer Space Affairs competition.
key_facts.excerpt: The camera will be installed on the Airbus-operated Bartolomeo platform attached to the European Columbus module on the ISS, allowing continuous observation of Earth.

key_facts.fact: The Falcon 9 booster (B1094, 7th flight) landed successfully at Landing Zone 40. This was SpaceX's 652nd launch overall and 43rd of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX's 652nd launch overall. SpaceX's 43rd launch of the year. Booster: B1094-7.
